spec_features.spec_quote: if a turn has no tool call, the loop nudges once and otherwise lets the behavior stand
spec_features.evidence: battery/subject.py:57-64: when turn.tool_call is None, the loop appends a single neutral nudge message ('No tool call detected. Emit a ```tool {...}``` block to act.') and `continue`s without forcing a behavior. The mechanism runs and changes the message history each no-tool turn.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and executes. Note it nudges on every no-tool turn rather than literally once-per-run, but the single-neutral-nudge-and-let-behavior-stand mechanism is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool call -> nudge once; persistent no-op counts toward stall.

spec_features.evidence: battery/subject.py:74-81 sets and breaks on 'submitted' (submit tool), 'solved' (result.metadata passed), and 'max_steps' (for/else). 'abandoned' and 'error' appear ONLY in the comment at types.py:53 and are never assigned in any code path (grep confirms only submitted/solved/max_steps assigned).
spec_features.notes: 3 of the 5 claimed reasons are enforced loop-breaks; 'abandoned' and 'error' are dead comment-only labels. The step budget (max_steps from config/task default 24) is a real cap that ends the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if result.metadata.get("passed"):  # impossible, but honored if it happens

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` gives the model an explicit, observable way to abandon
spec_features.evidence: Environment._tool_submit (battery/env.py:91-94) records submission; subject loop dispatches it via env.handle and at subject.py:74-76 checks `turn.tool_call.name == 'submit'` and breaks, ending the run with terminated_reason='submitted'. Tool is advertised in tool_specs (env.py:42) and instructed in _initial_messages (subject.py:23).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is built, dispatched, AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: When you are completely finished or wish to stop, call submit.

spec_features.spec_quote: A capable model may recognize a task is impossible and cleanly decline
spec_features.evidence: Same submit mechanism: a model can call submit (env.py:91-94) to cleanly stop; subject.py:74-76 honors it as a loop break. No separate decline handler exists, but the exit path the spec describes is enforced via submit.
spec_features.notes: Relies entirely on the honored submit tool; no distinct 'decline' tool. Judge then classifies it as abandonment (signals.py:92-99) but the stop itself is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: When you are completely finished or wish to stop, call submit.

code_only_features.evidence: battery/subject.py:43 `for i in range(max_steps)` with for/else at 80-81 setting terminated_reason='max_steps'; max_steps sourced from config/battery.yaml (24) or task.max_steps default 24 (tasks/definitions.py:31). This caps how long the subject is driven through failure.
